title: Collision models: Markovian and Non-Markovian impurity models
abstract: Collision models provide a flexible framework for studying open quantum systems and introducing non-Markovianity. We present a novel class of collision models, which we term Markovian impurity models, motivated by physical scenarios in which information backflow is periodically blocked. Using the Breuer-Laine-Piilo (BLP) measure of non-Markovianity, we show that if a $p$-impurity model is non-Markovian, then the corresponding $(p+1)$-impurity model is also non-Markovian, implying the existence of a critical $p$ at which the process transitions from Markovian to non-Markovian. Numerical simulations are used to investigate how this critical parameter depends on the system-ancilla and ancilla-ancilla interaction strengths. We find that, altough exceptions exist, increasing either interaction strength generally lowers the critical $p$, while sufficiently weak ancilla-ancilla interactions lead to a regime in which the dynamics remain Markovian even in the absence of impurities. Finally, we briefly introduce the complementary non-Markovian impurity model.
summary: This paper develops and analyzes a novel Markovian impurity model within the framework of collision models to study open quantum systems. Using the BLP measure, the authors establish a critical impurity parameter $p'$ that marks the transition point from Markovian to non-Markovian dynamics. The results show that interaction strengths can tune this critical point, offering deeper insight into the environmental memory effects in quantum dynamics.
main_problem: The paper investigates the non-Markovian nature of open quantum systems modeled by collision models, specifically focusing on a novel class called Markovian impurity models.
main_result: The authors prove that non-Markovianity propagates: if a $p$-impurity model is non-Markovian, the $(p+1)$-impurity model is also non-Markovian, establishing a critical impurity parameter $p'$ that dictates the transition from Markovian to non-Markovian dynamics.
method: The non-Markovianity is quantified using the Breuer-Laine-Piilo (BLP) measure, and the analysis involves comparing the dynamics of $p$-impurity models against $(p+1)$-impurity models.
model_or_system: The system uses Collision Models (CMs) where the environment interaction is modeled via sequential ancilla interactions. The focus is on the Markovian impurity model, defined by alternating evolution steps involving system-ancilla ($U_{XY}$) and ancilla-ancilla ($U_{YY}$) interactions.
key_observables: Non-Markovianity quantified by the BLP measure ($N_{BLP}$) and the change in trace distance ($\Delta D(t)$).
important_parameters: The impurity parameter ($p$), the critical $p'$ value, and the interaction strengths ($	heta_{XY}$ and $	heta_{YY}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes time-independent unitaries and uses the BLP measure to diagnose non-Markovianity. Numerical simulations are limited to $p \le 40$.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the dependence of the critical $p'$ on interaction strengths ($	heta_{XY}$ and $	heta_{YY}$), showing how increasing these strengths generally lowers $p'$, and also plot the asymptotic value of $	heta_{YY}$ where the process remains Markovian.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the collision model framework and the Markovian impurity model. It then uses the BLP measure to establish the relationship between $p$ and non-Markovianity, culminating in numerical investigations of how interaction strengths tune the critical parameter $p'$.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous theoretical tool (the critical $p$) to characterize when complex open quantum dynamics, modeled by sequential environmental coupling, transition from simple Markovian behavior to complex non-Markovian regimes, which is crucial for quantum memory and computation.
